title: Beginner Granny Square
description: A simple starter square you can join into blankets, bags, or cardigans.
licenseNote: Adapted from commonly shared free granny-square methods.
instructions: Make a magic ring and chain 3 (counts as first double crochet).
Work 2 double crochets into the ring, chain 2.
Repeat (3 double crochets, chain 2) three more times into the ring.
Pull ring tail to close center and slip stitch to top of beginning chain-3.
For round 2, slip stitch to corner space, chain 3, then work (2 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in same corner.
Work 3 dc in each side space and (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in each corner around.
Fasten off and weave in ends when square reaches desired size.

title: Simple Crochet Dishcloth
description: A quick rectangle pattern great for learning consistent tension.
licenseNote: Based on basic free dishcloth stitch patterns.
instructions: Chain 31 for a small square dishcloth.
Row 1: Single crochet in second chain from hook and each chain across.
Chain 1 and turn at the end of each row.
Rows 2-30: Single crochet in each stitch across.
Check shape; add or remove rows for a near-square cloth.
Fasten off leaving a small tail.
Weave in all ends and block lightly if needed.

title: Easy Everyday Beanie
description: Warm beginner-friendly beanie worked in rounds with a fast finish.
licenseNote: Inspired by common free beanie constructions.
instructions: Create a foundation chain that fits around the head comfortably with slight stretch.
Row 1: Half double crochet in each chain across.
Rows 2 onward: Work hdc in back loop only for rib texture.
Continue until panel length matches head circumference.
Slip stitch short ends together to make a tube.
Thread yarn through top edge stitches, pull tight to close crown.
Secure, weave ends, and add pom if desired.

title: Classic Textured Scarf
description: A relaxing row-repeat scarf pattern for everyday wear.
licenseNote: Adapted from classic beginner scarf stitch repeats.
instructions: Chain to desired scarf width, usually 26-34 stitches.
Row 1: Single crochet across.
Row 2: Alternate single crochet and double crochet across for texture.
Repeat row 2 until scarf reaches desired length.
Maintain even edge tension by counting stitches each row.
Fasten off and weave in ends.
Optional: Add fringe at both ends.

title: Ripple Baby Blanket
description: Soft ripple stitch pattern ideal for a nursery blanket.
licenseNote: Built from standard ripple blanket stitch structure.
instructions: Chain a multiple that supports ripple repeats plus turning stitches.
Row 1: Work dc pattern with increases at peaks and decreases at valleys.
Keep markers at each peak and valley to maintain shape.
Repeat ripple row sequence, changing colors every 2-4 rows if desired.
Continue until blanket reaches target length.
Add a simple border of single crochet around all sides.
Weave in ends and block for even edges.

title: Mesh Market Tote
description: Reusable mesh tote with strong handles and stretch.
licenseNote: Based on free mesh market tote constructions.
instructions: Begin with an oval or rectangular base using single crochet rounds.
Build 4-6 rounds for base stability.
Transition to mesh: chain 1, skip 1, dc in next stitch around.
Repeat mesh rounds until tote reaches desired height.
Work 2-3 solid rounds of single crochet at top edge.
Create handles by chaining spaces and reinforcing with sc rounds.
Fasten off and weave in all ends securely.

title: Mini Amigurumi Octopus
description: Small stuffed octopus project with basic shaping techniques.
licenseNote: Simple in-site amigurumi mini pattern for practice.
instructions: Round 1: Magic ring, 6 single crochet into ring.
Round 2: Increase in each stitch (12).
Round 3: (sc, inc) around (18).
Rounds 4-8: Single crochet around evenly.
Add safety eyes or embroider face before closing.
Stuff firmly and decrease rounds to close body.
Crochet tentacles separately and stitch to base.

title: Light Lace Shawl
description: Airy triangular shawl with lace repeats and drape.
licenseNote: Educational in-site lace shawl outline pattern.
instructions: Start with a magic ring and chain setup for a triangle shawl center.
Work increase points at center and both edges each row.
Alternate lace rows (chain spaces) with anchor rows (single crochet).
Track repeats with markers to avoid misaligned lace motifs.
Continue repeats until shawl wingspan is desired.
Finish with a decorative picot or shell border.
Wet block and pin to open lace pattern fully.

title: Retro Daisy Granny Square
licenseNote: Imported from the site owner’s personal library.
instructions: Row 1: Magic Ring, SCx8, sl.st [8]
Row 2: Chx3(Counts as 1DC), Dc, Dc incx7 [16]
Row 3: Change a new yarn color, Chx3(Counts as 1DC), Dc inc into the same ST, [Ch, Sk, Dcx3 into the next ST]x7, Ch, Sk, sl.st. [24]

Row 4: Change a new yarn color, Pull the yarn out of the loop with a slip stitch through the skipped stitches in the round2. Chx3 (Counts as 1DC), Chx4, Sk over to the next Sk St of round2, Dc, [Chx4, Sk over to the next Sk St of round2]x7, Sl.st [40]

Round 5: Switching back to the round3 yarn color, Pull the loop from the round4 Ch space to place it in front of the round3, Chx3 (Counts as 1DC), [2 dc in next st (from Round 3), 1 dc in last st of cluster] while keeping Round 4 ch stitches pushed to the back. Repeat: [Chx2, skip 1 dc from Round 4, 1 dc in next st, 2 dc in next st, 1 dc in next st] around. End with Ch 2 and sl.st into the top of ch 3.

Round 6: Switch back to the yarn color from Round 4. Pull up a loop to the front in any ch1 sp. Ch 3 (counts as the first dc), 1 dc in the same st. Repeat:[Ch 5, skip 4 dc, 2 dc in the next dc from Round 4] around. End with ch 5 and sl.st into the top of the ch 3.

Round 7: Switch back to the yarn color from Round 5. Pull up a loop to the front in any ch5 sp from Round 6. Insert hook through the ch spaces of Round 6 and pull the loop from Round 5 to the front. Chx3 (counts as the first dc). 2 dc in the next st of Round 5. 1 dc in the next 2 sts of the cluster. Repeat:[Ch 2, skip the 2 dc from Round 6, 1 dc in the next st, 2 dc in the next st, 1 dc in the next 2 sts] around. End with ch 2 and sl st into the top of the ch 3.

Round 8: Continue with the same yarn. Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Sc in the first st, sk 1 st, 5 dc in the next st (center dc of the cluster), sk 1 st, sc in the next st. Repeat: [Ch 2, sk the ch-2 space from Round 7, sc in the first st of the next dc cluster, sk 1 st, 5 dc in the next st, sk 1 st, sc in the last st of the dc cluster] around. End with ch 2 and sl.st into the first sc.

Round 9: Switch back to the yarn color from Round 7. Pull the yarn to the front. Chx3 (counts as the first dc).Work 2 dc in the next st from Round 7. Flip the flower petal (Round 8) downward and work 5 dc into the ch space from Round 7 behind the petal. Flip the petal back up. Work 1 dc in the first dc st and 2 dc in the next dc st in front of the petal (from Round 8). Repeat: [Flip the petal down, work 5 dc in the ch space from Round 7, flip the petal back up, work 1 dc in the first st and 2 dc in the next st in front of the petal] around. End with a sl.st into the top of the starting ch-3.

Round 10: Chx1 (does not count as a st), Sc in the first st. Sc in the next 5 sts. Hdc in the next st. Dc in the next st. Corner: Work (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in the next st. Dc in the next st. Hdc in the next st. Sc in the next 11 sts. Hdc in the next st. Dc in the next st. Corner: Work (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in the next st. Dc in the next st. Hdc in the next st. Sc in the next 11 sts. Hdc in the next st. Dc in the next st. Corner: Work (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in the next st. Dc in the next st. Hdc in the next st. Sc in the next 11 sts. Hdc in the next st. Dc in the next st. Corner: Work (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in the next st. Dc in the next st. Hdc in the next st. Sc in the last 5 sts. Sl st into the first sc to join.

Round 11: CHx1 (does not count as a stitch) Hdc into the next 9 sts In the corner CH 2 sp, work (2 DC, CH 2, 2 DC) Hdc into the next 19 sts In the corner CH 2 sp, work (2 DC, CH 2, 2 DC) Hdc into the next 19 sts In the corner CH 2 sp, work (2 DC, CH 2, 2 DC) Hdc into the next 19 sts In the corner CH 2 sp, work (2 DC, CH 2, 2 DC) Hdc into the next 9 sts SL.ST into the first st Fasten off, cut yarn leaving 6-10 inches, and pull yarn tail through the last loop.
